作者当务之急是把地图，尤其是把POI这个基础游戏知识搞懂。 地图糙没问题，随机生成地图也没问题。但是你不能在不给地标建筑的情况下不做基本的地图系统。而作者不仅没做，取代的指南针系统也是存在误导性的。 我不明白为什么游戏里重要的指南针，指的不是地堡入口，而是更内部、且存在方位差异的地堡门口。这导致的一个直接结果就是：玩家无法从指南针中获取准确信息，反而会被误导。更糟糕的是，游戏中的异常风暴不存在任何预防措施，玩家不能提前通过某些方式去知晓大致的触发时间，从而去规划当日的搜刮行程。只能在防空警报响起时，尽快回到地堡。此时的指南针问题彻底暴露：指南针在这关键时刻无法发挥其功能，玩家对着指南针走，走到尽头却是一堵墙的一脸懵逼。 如果作者想刻意弱化玩家的方向感，强化指南针的作用。那么就麻烦把指南针系统做好。

I've been having a good time with this game so far. Been playing singleplayer, I love having difficulty options including a custom mode that allows you to tweak things to your liking. I know it's an odd thing to praise, but it's something that's missing from other co-op oriented games like Lethal Company and Repo. Very good for offline play. As for the game itself I love the aesthetic, the exploration of procedural environments, scavenging, and the sound design. The looming air raid siren as a Shining is about to roll in is phenomenal and I'm interested to see where future developments go. Hopefully there will be an option to get less bunkers on a high Shining count. While they are awesome, you can miss the open environments of rural and urban Zaslavie. It's also good on Steam Deck. Which I often bring to work to pass time on long delays with nothing else to do.

[h1]不推荐：很多地方还停留在粗糙阶段，开头玩法有新意，后面的太平淡了[/h1] 这游戏会吸引人的点: 核灾废土、合作生存、昼出夜归、地堡经营，再加上地图轮换， 游戏刚开始的时候，资源紧张、时间有限，还是可以的。尤其是前期那种三十秒内迅速搜寻物资这个创意点挺不错的 但问题在于，这个亮点并没有被后续内容很好地支撑起来。玩得越久，越能感觉到这游戏的问题不是“难”，而是[b]重复、粗糙，而且不够尊重玩家时间[/b]。 1. [b]引导和信息传达做得很差。[/b] 地图不小，却没有一个足够直观的地图系统，唯一能依赖的指南针也很模糊。场景一旦复杂一点，或者你稍微绕一下路，就很容易失去方向感。很多时候死掉是因为找不到方向，游戏没有把足够清晰的信息给玩家。对新手来说，提高了很多理解成本。 后续优化推荐可以针对基地和捡尸做一个可选开启的方向指引 2. [b]死亡后的捡尸体验非常糟糕。[/b] 生存游戏有死亡惩罚很正常，但的问题是惩罚经常直接越过“紧张”，变成“劝退”。连续死几次之后，尸体掉到远处、偏门位置，加上没有地图系统，几次之后你根本不想再跑一遍的地方，前面的搜刮成果基本等于白搭。 这种设计不是让人想更谨慎，而是让人觉得：算了，不想继续了。 3. [b]前期搜刮有意思，后期搜刮很无聊。[/b] 玩到后面，体验很容易退化成重复地出门、搜东西、回家、整理、再出门。流程越来越像机械劳动，而不是生存冒险。 4. [b]敌人 AI 和整体遭遇感也比较重复。[/b] [h2]总结[/h2] 这游戏不是完全没有优点。 它的题材选得很好，氛围也确实做出来了，前期那种限时搜刮资源的节奏相当不错。 但也正因为它有这些优点，后面暴露出来的问题才更可惜。 它现在给我的感觉不是“太真实所以不适合我”，而是[b]有潜力，但完成度和打磨程度还撑不起它想做的体验[/b]。 如果以后能把引导、地图指向、死亡回收、后期重复度，以及敌人 AI/遭遇设计这些地方认真优化，我觉得它是有机会变得更好的。 但以目前这个版本来说，我只能给出[b]不推荐[/b]。

I really wanted to like this game because the atmosphere, retro PS2-style visuals, and general survival vibe are great. The world feels interesting and there’s definitely something compelling about the setting. However, the combat completely killed the experience for me. After about 7 hours of gameplay on the easiest difficulty, I finally obtained a Mosin-Nagant expecting it to feel like a meaningful upgrade from melee combat. Instead, I encountered an unarmored human enemy at point blank range, and it took four headshots to kill him. That completely destroyed any sense of weapon progression or satisfaction. The Mosin should feel powerful and rewarding for accurate shots, but instead it felt weak even in the most ideal conditions possible. I don’t mind difficult or survival focused games, but this crossed the line from challenging into frustrating. It made combat feel inconsistent and unrewarding, which is a huge problem in a game that relies so heavily on survival encounters. If the weapon balance or damage consistency were improved, this could be a much stronger experience, because the atmosphere and idea behind the game are genuinely good.

I DO recommend this game, and it really is fun, but the amount of bugs me and my friend encountered during our playthrough makes me set this review as not recommended. I love many aspects of this game; the gritty atmosphere, the sound design, and the stylization. I honestly think it's great, but it gets ruined by the amount of glitches and bugs that quickly break the immersion. The physics also feel way to unrefined and rigid, and sometimes things won't even load. During our most recent continuation of my friends save, we encountered a map with ZERO collision. On my friends end, he saw no map at all, but on my end the map 'seemed' to be completely loaded. I told him it's probably the games jankness or something and ran straight into the forest ahead... before falling into the floor and dying. Ruined the whole game for me, if the devs fix these bugs, it would genuinely be an 8/10 or a 9/10 game. Right now it would sit at around 5/10. If you can tolerate the bugs (and have a friend to play with), please do purchase the game and support the devs so they can continue developing it. If not, its much better to save your money until the game gets the big fix it needs.

[h3]Intro[/h3] I am someone who plays a lot of under the radar indie games, mainly to support indie developers but also with the hopes I may find a true diamond in the rough. This game caught my attention with some a good art style alongside appealing retro graphics (something I am a big fan of), so when my friend wanted to buy the game to play together, I bit and gave it a shot. However, after playing with a friend for about two days for a few hours it is apparent the retro graphics are basically the only enjoyable thing this game offers. [h3]Dislikes[/h3] The game is just plain not fun. It is set in a nuclear wasteland in which survival is meant to be really difficult, but survival is actually the easiest part of the game and requires basically no effort. Food, water, and radiation are incredibly easy to manage, and the biggest challenge with regards to it is knowing you are starving/dehydrated in the first place (since the game does not display this data on your HUD). Radiation also goes away incredibly quickly so there is no real downside to drinking irradiated water, so long as you don't do it all at once. The lack of good survival mechanics it a huge downside for this game, as since it has no meaningful progression or story to complete, these mechanics need to be engaging enough to compensate. This is not the case with this game, and the janky controls and sometimes obtuse mechanics don't help with that one bit. One such obtuse mechanic is the Sirzez. Selling things in the Sirzez is a huge hassle because this game has some of the most random buy/sell restrictions I've seen in any game. There is a guy you can buy ammo from guns from, but for some reason you can only sell rusty weapons to? Why can't I sell ammo for guns I don't have yet? Most of the Sirzez is like this, only taking very specific (and often otherwise useful) materials for selling, while leaving your base with useless junk that you have to get rid of manually. The combat in this game isn't much better. The enemies are so incredibly basic I feel confident saying I've coded better enemies in Unity myself, they all just run directly towards you and attack if in range. If they have a gun they shoot you, but its very easy to tank the damage and kill them with melee anyways (and of course the ones with guns don't drop guns because why would they). The game is also incredibly buggy, especially for my friend who I played coop with, as he encountered constant controller issues and a strange bug in which he kept on getting radiation poisoning even after respawning (this made the game unplayable for him). I cannot speak on that as the bugs did not effect me nearly as much as him, but I did encounter things such as ghost items in my inventory taking up space. Finally, exploring is a huge pain since you always need to mind the "Shinings" that occur on a regular basis. Shinings basically force you to go back to base or you die, and while on paper it sounds like a fun mechanic most of the time it just interrupts whatever you were doing and takes away some of the fun inherent in exploring the world [h3]Likes[/h3] The only part of this game I actively enjoyed were the retro graphics and the anomalies, but even my enjoyment of them comes with caveats. Anomalous occurrences are so common that they lost their charm quick, and many (like the black holes) cause graphical glitches not related to the anomaly. The places in the thumbnails when you load up the game look pretty cool but because of graphical glitches they rarely look how they do in the title screen when you find them in game. [h3]Feedback[/h3] As far as feedback goes, this game desperately needs something that sets it apart, as it is very similar to the game S.T.A.L.K.E.R. The retro artstyle is a start, but it is nowhere near enough when many of the core mechanics are below the average I would expect for a release of a standalone small indie title, let alone something that plans to compete with S.T.A.L.K.E.R. This game desperately needs bug fixes, polished mechanics, a tighter gameplay loop, and overall just more content before I could ever seriously recommend it. [h3]Final Score[/h3] 3/10

MISERY has a great atmosphere and some really interesting ideas, but after playing it as a group of three, we all ended up sharing the same frustration: the overall game balancing. The biggest issue for us was the loot system and the economy. Finding valuable items, managing resources, and making progress often felt more tedious than rewarding, with the balance between effort and reward not quite feeling right. There is definitely a lot of potential here, especially with its oppressive atmosphere and survival elements, but the uneven economy and progression made it difficult for us to fully enjoy the experience.

Very arcadey. If you're looking for a game that actually fulfills the experience of STALKER, that being tense survival and gunfights, please look elsewhere. Everyone is a bullet sponge, enemies don't actually drop the things they're carrying (enemies carrying guns and melee weapons just drop generic loot), and the maps are very small. It would be more interesting if the random generation generated a world, instead of a tiny arena for you to run around in. Maybe fun with friends, but what game isn't? I played solo and it was certainly very boring in such a case. An unfortunate turn of events, because the idea of a true survival game where you have to build your own shelter within a STALKER kind of exclusion zone is quite an interesting one, but this game executes it very poorly.

Also, grab the mannequins so you can set up different load outs depending on the map. Bunkers are always heavily radiated so I wear specific gear just for them versus standard field map. Overall, my only advice for the developers are give me more updates!
